$comment: The scenetake scenario format for editors. tests/Scenetake.Tests/ScenarioSchemaTests.cs keeps its keys and names in step with the code, and checks every sample and fixture against it. Spec: .github/docs/spec_scenario.md → Editor schema.
title: scenetake scenario
description: A scenetake scenario: the commands that scenetake types and runs for a terminal recording, and how the recording looks. Only steps is required.

title.description: The recording's title. The window's title bar shows it, unless render.window-title gives another text.

height.description: Terminal rows. By default the image leaves out empty rows below the output (render.fit).

cwd.description: The folder that pre, steps, and post start in. A relative path starts at this file's folder. Default: the folder scenetake runs in. The folder must exist.

shell.description: The shell for every command: bash, pwsh, powershell, or a path. Default: $SHELL, and pwsh on Windows. On Windows, bash is Git Bash. With bash, zsh, and PowerShell, a cd or an export carries to the next steps.

outputs.description: The files a recording writes besides the cast, each with its own format and options: a dark and a light SVG for a README, a GIF for Zenn, an mp4 for X. Written when no --format is given.

pre.description: Commands that run before the steps and are not recorded. With bash, zsh, and PowerShell, their folder and variables carry to the steps.

steps.description: The commands to record, in order. A step is a command, or a mapping with run and the step keys, or a card or clear step.

post.description: Commands that run after the steps and are not recorded. They also run when the recording stops with an error.

style.description: A style: a color name (red, bright-cyan, gray), tokens such as "bold underline fg:yellow bg:blue", fg:/bg: with a name, 0-255, #rrggbb, or r,g,b, or a raw SGR such as 1;31. none keeps the text plain. Quote a style with #.

hexColor.errorMessage: A color is #rgb or #rrggbb, in quotes: YAML reads # after a space as a comment.

anyOf.errorMessage: Unknown theme. scenetake --help lists the themes.

windowName.description: A title bar around the terminal: none, macos, or windows.

anyOf.errorMessage: A window is none, macos, or windows.

fitMode.description: Which edges move in to the last row and column the recording uses: height (the default: no empty rows below), width, both, or none (the whole terminal).

anyOf.errorMessage: fit is none, height, width, or both.

outputFormat.description: svg, mp4, gif, or png. Every recording also writes the cast. mp4 and gif need ffmpeg.

anyOf.errorMessage: format is svg, mp4, gif, or png. The cast is always written.

showValue.description: What the recording shows of the step: all (the prompt, the typed command, and the output), output (the output only), or none (nothing: a step that prepares the next ones).

anyOf.errorMessage: show is all, output, or none.

keyName.description: A key: enter, tab, space, backspace, escape, up, down, left, right, home, end, page-up, page-down, insert, delete, f1-f12, ctrl+ and a letter (ctrl+c), or alt+ and a character (alt+x).

anyOf.errorMessage: Unknown key name. Text to type goes in type, not key.

lineRange.description: Lines and columns, 1-based: 3 (line 3), 2-5 (lines 2 to 5), 4- (line 4 to the end), 2:7-10 (columns 7 to 10 of line 2), 2:12- (column 12 to the end of line 2).

settings.description: Defaults for every step. A map-form step can change each timing and color key for itself.

prompt.description: Shown before each typed command, and at the end. Text, or a list of parts, each text or {text, color}. {dir} shows the name of the folder the step starts in.

text.description: The part's text. {dir} shows the folder's name.

typing-jitter.description: Random variance (+/- seconds) per typed character.

pre-delay.description: Seconds before a step is typed.

post-delay.description: Seconds after a step's output, before the next step.

end-prompt.description: End with the prompt after the last output, as a terminal does. By default the recording ends on the last output.

execution-duration.description: Seconds after Enter before the output appears, at least.

stream-output.description: Play the output at the times it came, instead of all at once.

max-duration.description: Fit each step's output into at most this many seconds. Turns stream-output on.

silence-threshold.description: Stream output: a pause longer than this many seconds is shortened to max-idle.

max-idle.description: Stream output: the seconds a long pause is shortened to.

stderr-color.description: The color of stderr that has no colors of its own. none keeps it plain (git and many tools print progress on stderr).

mask.description: Texts to hide as * wherever the recording shows them, such as a host name.

mask-auto.description: Hide what looks like a secret: tokens, KEY=value secrets, passwords in URLs, private keys, and the values of secret environment variables.

mask-personal.description: Hide the user name, home folder name, computer name, and git name and email of the machine that records.

render.description: How the SVG, mp4, GIF, and PNG look. The cast keeps it too, so scenetake svg, mp4, gif, and png draw the cast the same way later. Command-line options such as --theme override it.

font-family.description: A CSS font-family list, such as '"JetBrains Mono", monospace'. An SVG uses the viewer's fonts.

window-title.description: The title bar's text. Default: title. "" shows none.

background.description: The fill around the window: a color ("#1e3c72"), 2-4 colors for a gradient ("#1e3c72 #2a5298"), or a .png, .jpg, .gif, or .webp file relative to this file. Quote a color.

margin.description: Pixels around the terminal or window. Default 8, 12 with a window, 32 with a background.

padding.description: Pixels between the terminal's edge and its text. Default: from font-size.

opacity.description: How much of the window covers the background image or gradient, 0-1. Text stays opaque. Needs background.

blur.description: Pixels of blur on the background seen through a window with opacity below 1.

loop.description: false plays the SVG and the GIF once and stops on the final screen.

end-hold.description: Seconds the final screen stays before the SVG starts again or the video ends. Default: as long as the pause before the last output.

fade-out.description: Seconds over which the text fades out after end-hold. The window and the background stay.

speed.description: How many times as fast as recorded the SVG, mp4, and GIF play. The cast keeps the recorded times. Not with length.

length.description: The most seconds the SVG, mp4, and GIF play: waits in the output shrink first, then pauses, then typing, each only down to what stays readable. A shorter recording stays as it is. The cast keeps the recorded times. Not with speed.

length.errorMessage: speed and length both set how long the output plays: keep one.

crop.description: Rows or columns cut from that edge before fit.

theme.description: The color theme: a preset, with single colors changed on top of it.

fg.description: The text color, #rgb or #rrggbb, in quotes.

bg.description: The background color, #rgb or #rrggbb, in quotes.

palette.description: The 16 ANSI colors, each #rgb or #rrggbb, separated by :, in quotes.
palette.errorMessage: palette is 16 colors, each #rgb or #rrggbb, separated by :.

output.description: A file to write besides the cast. The other keys are the command-line options of the same name, without --, for this file only.

length.errorMessage: speed and length both set how long the file plays: keep one.

file.description: The file name, relative to the folder of the outputs. The extension may be left out. Default: the scenario's name. Two entries of one format need a file each.

window-title.description: The title bar's text. "" shows none.

background.description: A color, 2-4 colors for a gradient, or an image file relative to this file.

margin.description: Pixels around the terminal or window.

padding.description: Pixels between the terminal's edge and its text.

opacity.description: How much of the window covers the background, 0-1.

blur.description: Pixels of blur on the background seen through the window.

font-size.description: Font size in pixels. A smaller font makes a smaller GIF.

loop.description: false plays the SVG or the GIF once.

fade-out.description: Seconds over which the text fades out after end-hold.

speed.description: How many times as fast as recorded this file plays, 0.25-4, such as 1.5 or 2x.

length.description: The most seconds this file plays, 1-600, such as 15 or 15s. Not with speed.

at.description: svg and png: one screen, the one shown this many seconds into the recording, or end for the final screen.

max-fps.description: svg: cap the animation's frame rate. 0 keeps every frame.

fps.description: mp4 and gif: frames per second. Default 30 for mp4 and 20 for a GIF, at most 50.

crf.description: mp4: H.264 quality. A higher value makes a smaller file. Default 23.

max-size.description: mp4 and gif: scale down to fit in WxH, keeping the shape. 1280x1024 fits X.

size.description: mp4 and gif: WxH makes the video exactly that size (both even), the terminal centered on the theme's background. W:H, such as 16:9, pads it to that shape at the terminal's own size, which max-size can then scale down.

font-file.description: mp4, gif, and png: a font file (TTF, OTF, TTC) to draw with first.

propertyNames.errorMessage: An svg entry takes no fps, crf, max-size, size, or font-file: those are for mp4 and gif (font-file also png), and an SVG takes max-fps.
A png entry is one screen: it takes no max-fps, fps, crf, max-size, or size.
An mp4 entry plays the whole recording: it takes no at or max-fps. Use fps for its frame rate.
A gif entry plays the whole recording and has no H.264 quality: it takes no at, max-fps, or crf. Use fps for its frame rate.

keyEntry.description: One thing to do while the command runs, in this order: sleep, then wait, then type or key.

wait.description: Wait until the output shows this text, such as a prompt. Steadier than sleep on a slower machine. Gives up after the step's timeout, or 10 seconds.

type.description: Text to type, one character at a time at typing-speed. A line break is Enter.

propertyNames.errorMessage: An entry has type or key, not both: put the key in the next entry.

highlight.description: Colors part of the step's output.

at.description: Where: a range of lines and columns, or a list of them.

step.description: A command to type and run, or a mapping: run with step keys, a card, or a clear step.

run.description: The command. Quote a command that contains ": ".

name.description: A comment line shown before the command, with an optional [style] prefix: "[bright-yellow]Build it".

typing-speed.description: Average seconds per typed character, for this step.

typing-jitter.description: Random variance (+/- seconds) per typed character, for this step.

pre-delay.description: Seconds before this step is typed.

post-delay.description: Seconds after this step's output. A card stays this long, 2 by default.

execution-duration.description: Seconds after Enter before the output appears, at least.

stream-output.description: Play the output at the times it came.

max-duration.description: Fit the output into at most this many seconds. Turns stream-output on.

silence-threshold.description: Stream output: a pause longer than this is shortened to max-idle.

max-idle.description: Stream output: the seconds a long pause is shortened to.

run-highlight.description: The style of the typed command.

highlight.description: Colors for parts of the output, by line and column. On a pty step, by the lines the program writes, over its own colors. Not for interactive steps.

stderr-color.description: The color of stderr that has no colors of its own, for this step. Not with pty: true, where stdout and stderr are one stream.

pty.description: Run in a pseudo-terminal: for TUIs, progress bars, and tools that color only for a terminal. Needed for keys.

interactive.description: You use the program yourself while it records. Needs pty: true. scenetake --save-keys saves your keys as keys entries.

normalize-typing.description: With interactive: true, type your keys at typing-speed and drop Backspace corrections.

continue-on-error.description: The command is meant to fail: no warning for its exit code, also with --strict.

keys.description: Keys scenetake writes to the program while it runs, in order. Needs pty: true.

timeout.description: Seconds after which scenetake stops the command: Ctrl+C in a PTY. Not a failure.

clear.description: Clear the screen, as clear does, without running a command.

card.description: Lines shown centered on a cleared screen, without running a command: a title, or an install line at the end. Each line may start with a [style] prefix.

background.description: Start the command and go on while it runs, such as a server that later steps call. It is not recorded, and stops at the end.

wait.description: With background: true, start the next step when the command prints this text, such as "Listening on".

wait-timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the wait text. Default 30.

keep-output.description: Show this step's output from the earlier cast when recording again, even when it changed, such as a date. The command still runs.

rerun.description: false shows this step's output from the earlier cast without running the command: a slow step, one that costs money or changes something, or an interactive step recorded once by hand. Its cd and export do not happen then. It runs when the earlier cast does not have it, and with --rerun.

propertyNames.errorMessage: A card step takes card, pre-delay, and post-delay only.
A clear step takes clear, name, pre-delay, and post-delay only.
A background step takes run, wait, wait-timeout, and continue-on-error only: it is not recorded.
keys and timeout do not apply to interactive: true, where a person types and ends the step.
show: none shows nothing and takes no time, so it takes no name, highlight, stderr-color, delay, output timing, keep-output, or rerun.
show: output types nothing, so run-highlight has no effect.
